item.title: Cylinder Spectrum & Polygon Plexus — Mon Oct 19, 12:00 PM — 918 Bathurst Arts and Culture Center
item.description:
"Cylinder Spectrum" & "Polygon Plexus" are two visual art exhibitions by Toronto artist Angela Julian (Native Torontonian and OCADU graduate). Both shows are located inside the Sun Gallery at 918 Bathurst Arts & Culture Center. The collected works are a group of large scale colorful abstract paintings done in plaster. They range in size, scale, shape, and number, but they are all tied together through the mediums of plaster and acrylic paint.
On one side of the gallery is the show "Cylinder Spectrum", which is a group of acrylic paintings done on distinctly rounded canvases that were covered in layers of mixed-media and plaster. These are shown both as individual works and presented as a group that makeup a larger installation. The circular nature of the canvases and surfaces links the entire show by their rounded nature. On the opposite side of the gallery is the show "Polygon Plexus" which is a group of hand-made canvases and surfaces that were created to form irregular shapes. The

item.title: The Face is a Landscape — Mon Oct 19, 12:00 PM — 918 Bathurst Arts and Culture Center
item.description: "The Face is a Landscape" is a visual arts exhibition by Toronto artist Angela Julian. The large body of art features colorful works done in Portraiture. The show is comprised of drawings and paintings created in a highly-detailed contemporary style. She explores painterly and drawn techniques in both wet and dry mediums. The faces are designed using many layers of blended line-work, impressions, and cross-hatchings. She uses very fine brushes and drawing instruments to achieve these micro-techniques that makeup the broader whole of the picture. The works are located in the Star Gallery and fill up the room from floor to ceiling. The subjects of each portrait are all well-known authors, writers, or philosophers by nature. Angela is penning her first book series in the high-fantasy genre, she has included portraits in the show based on writers that had a direct impact on her as a reader and aspiring author. The exhibition is largely a homage to those writers and thinkers who influenced

item.title: 🍂 Fall Walk: Rouge National Urban Park and Picnic🌳 — Sat Oct 24, 9:45 AM
item.description:
Toronto Movies & Social Group - Celebrating 14 Years! # 🍂🌳 Fall Walk: Rouge National Urban Park 🌳🍁
### A Real Hike, Beautiful Fall Colours & a Picnic Together
Want to get out of the city without actually leaving Toronto?
**Rouge National Urban Park** is Canada's only urban national park — and one of the most popular hikes we do. Once you get onto the trail, it can be hard to believe you're still in Toronto. Forest paths, rolling hills, changing leaves, and quiet stretches of wilderness make this feel much more like a trip outside the city than a walk through it. And fall is one of the best times to experience it.
This is **a real hike**, though. There are some hills and ups and downs, so it isn't the best choice if you're looking for an easy, flat walk. But if you're up for the challenge, there's something satisfying about reaching the end knowing you did it together. And then we'll have a picnic. 🧺

item.title: 🍂🌿 NEW FALL WALK: Discover Biidaasige Park 🌿🍂 — Sun Oct 25, 11:00 AM
item.description:
Try New Things in Toronto! # 🍂🌿 **NEW FALL WALK: Discover Biidaasige Park** 🌿🍂
### A Brand-New Toronto Park, Fall Colours & Waterfront Trails
We're trying something **new**!
Join us for our first group walk to **Biidaasige Park**, one of the newest and most ambitious parks in Toronto. Opened as part of the massive transformation of the Port Lands, the park sits on **Ookwemin Minising**, Toronto's new island where the Don River meets Lake Ontario.
This isn't a walk we've done before, which makes it a little more exciting. We'll spend much of the afternoon actually **exploring the park rather than rushing through it** — following its trails, enjoying the waterfront, taking in the fall scenery, and stopping along the way to appreciate the new landscape. The park is enormous, with more than **50 acres already open** and more sections being added as the Port Lands transformation continues.

item.title: The Face is a Landscape — Tue Oct 27, 12:00 PM — 918 Bathurst Arts and Culture Center
item.description: "The Face is a Landscape" is a visual arts exhibition by Toronto artist Angela Julian. The large body of art features colorful works done in Portraiture. The show is comprised of drawings and paintings created in a highly-detailed contemporary style. She explores painterly and drawn techniques in both wet and dry mediums. The faces are designed using many layers of blended line-work, impressions, and cross-hatchings. She uses very fine brushes and drawing instruments to achieve these micro-techniques that makeup the broader whole of the picture. The works are located in the Star Gallery and fill up the room from floor to ceiling. The subjects of each portrait are all well-known authors, writers, or philosophers by nature. Angela is penning her first book series in the high-fantasy genre, she has included portraits in the show based on writers that had a direct impact on her as a reader and aspiring author. item.title: Connection Beyond Breath: Living Relationships with Our Dead — Tue Oct 27, 7:00 PM — Online
item.description: Queer Death Salon is a virtual community space for all 2SLGBTQIA+ people to come together to discuss death, dying and grief. In this collective conversation, grievers are invited to connect over ways they are or want to be in relation with their dead. This is not an instructional session but rather a container for folks to share and hear about the variety of ways our dead show up in our lives - in dreams, memories, conversations, spaces, through animal sightings, cultural and spiritual practices, etc. - and how ongoing relationships with our dead can transform how we live, in tough, tender, and touching ways. Fueled by years of cultivating relationships with their dead, Case hopes participants leave this conversation both feeling more resourced to build and maintain relationships with theirs, and imagining how we, too, will want to be remembered and connected with when we join them. “Time is queer and so is grief: grief queers time inexorably. item.description: The Continental Philosophy Research Interest Group welcomes guest speaker Thimo Heisenberg, an associate professor in the Department of Philosophy at Rice University. Professor Heisenberg is a specialist in 19th and 20th century German Philosophy. Having earned his PhD from Columbia in 2019, his work has appeared in journals such as the British Journal of the History of Philosophy, the European Journal of Philosophy, Inquiry, and the Journal of the American Philosophical Association, as well as in many edited collections and anthologies. He was a Fulbright Scholar, and has received fellowships from the Alexander-von-Humboldt Foundation, the German National Academic Foundation, the Max Weber Program and from Columbia University. His book, The Economy in German Idealism, is under contract with Oxford University Press.
